item.title: When Telemetry Turns Predatory: A DevSecOps Look at Digital Repression in Venezuela
item.description: Every SOC pipeline has a shadow version. Using Venezuela as a grounded case study: how the primitives security engineers build become surveillance systems.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: Testing an IAM Analyzer Against Its Own Claims
item.description: I validated my client-side IAM blast-radius analyzer against a published catalog of privilege-escalation methods I did not write, and a harness that attacks its own tests. Twice, a green build hid a wrong answer.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: The DevSecOps Guide: Hardening, IAM, and Incident Response
item.description: A hub for the DevSecOps writing on rivassec.com: IAM blast radius, TLS, incident response, and controls that hold up in production.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: When the Output Carries the Signal: Claude, SynthID-Text, and the New Detection Attack Surface
item.description: Claude's planned text watermark is embedded through token selection rather than hidden characters. Once enterprises automate on its detector, that provenance feature becomes a security control plane with spoofing, evasion, oracle, key-management, supply-chain, and policy-abuse requirements.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: IAM Blast Radius Is an Architecture Problem, Not a Policy Problem
item.description: Most IAM reviews start too late, after the account structure and trust boundaries are set. Least privilege isn't fewer actions; it's smaller failure domains.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: The Discovery Layer Is Broken: Hiring as an Observability Problem
item.description: The senior engineering market has a routing failure, not a talent shortage: resumes and funnels index for keywords and discard the signal seniors depend on.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: Prompt Injection Will Become a Supply Chain Evasion Technique
item.description: Prompt injection's threat model is older than the term. The mechanism is new, the objective is the evasion goal attackers have pursued for decades.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: Bandit-Clean Pwnagotchi Plugins: How `subprocess` Goes From Risk to Routine
item.description: Hardening a Pwnagotchi plugin against Bandit B602/B603/B607: shutil.which() full paths, argv-list calls, input validation, and the nosec discipline.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: TLS Has Three Jobs. Forget the Rest.
item.description: TLS gets easier when you stop walking the handshake and name what it's for. It does three jobs; anchor those and it becomes design, not memorization.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: Adoption Is a Security Control: Notes from Paving a Road
item.description: A control developers route around isn't a control. Field notes on making the secure path the easy path: 40% less remediation time, 27% less pipeline latency.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: The Teensy That Failed in Public: An EFI Brute Force, Hours Late
item.description: In 2013 Hackaday called my MacBook EFI brute force a failure; hours later it worked. Three rate-limiting defenses, each leaking at a different seam.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: IAM Roles That Fail Loud: Small Defaults, Big Difference
item.description: A small Pulumi library that treats IAM safety as a precondition: mandatory permissions boundary, no wildcard trust, no wildcard actions, every opt-out explicit.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: The Trust Decay: Why Modern Hiring Has Become an Adversarial System
item.description: The tech hiring pipeline has shifted from talent discovery to risk mitigation. In 2026, the engineers who get hired are the ones who are hardest to doubt.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: Never Lose Connection: Multi-Phone Bluetooth Tethering for Pwnagotchi
item.description: bt-tether-multi is a Pwnagotchi plugin for intelligent multi-phone Bluetooth tethering with automatic WAN failover and silent-disconnect recovery in the field.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: Elasticsearch Snapshot Verification, Minimal Privileges
item.description: Verify Elasticsearch snapshots without manage_snapshot: minimal API key, Prometheus-friendly script, and a public tools repo for hardened monitoring automation.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: Hardening Kubernetes Deployments
item.description: Pod-level Kubernetes guardrails aligned with the Pod Security Standards Restricted profile: non-root, no caps, read-only FS, NetworkPolicies, SA hardening.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: Taming the OOM Killer: Process Priorities on Linux
item.description: The Linux OOM Killer decides what dies under memory pressure. Protect sshd, mysqld, and other critical processes with oom_score_adj via a small script.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: Catching a Nation-State Proxy: OSINT on Twitter
item.description: In 2012 I traced a state-aligned Twitter proxy tied to Venezuela's ruling party. OSINT lessons for spotting subtle, credential-phishing nation-state infra.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: The 208.5-Day Kernel Bug: Uptime, Overflow, and Risk
item.description: A 2012 Linux kernel bug caused CPU lockups after 208.5 days of uptime due to an integer overflow in sched_clock(). RHEL 5/6 lesson: patch and observe uptime.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas

item.title: The 2012 Leap Second: When Time Broke Java and the Cloud
item.description: The 2012 leap second broke Reddit, Yelp, Java apps, and more. A retrospective on how fragile timekeeping bit the cloud, and what SRE teams should do today.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Rivas
